# Sanity Audit Report

Audit date: 17 November 2026 (Asia/Calcutta). Read-only source audit; only this report is written. No build, lint, tests, TypeScript check, package installs, form requests, emails, Sanity Content Lake requests/writes, imports or deployment. Prior README changes were left untouched. Official documentation was consulted for proposed integrations.

Inventory: **29 editorial pages + 1 quote status page = 30 page URLs; 313 page-owned logical sections; 251 stored JSON sections; 10 proposed global singletons; 1 distinct active form.**

Counting: heroes, introductions, content sections, contact columns, gallery/review grids, FAQ topics, closing CTAs and status panels count. Nested maps/hours, CTA rows, marquee/trust panels, dividers and layout globals do not. Root-layout homepage closing CTA is a global. Recovery states are listed separately from stable page URLs. Counts reflect static render analysis of current local data, not live browser verification.

## Part A — Site analysis

### Every page and its sections in render order

Route groups do not appear in URLs. Home: src/app/(home)/page.tsx. Dynamic root route: src/app/(content)/[slug]/page.tsx, 26 current content slugs, dynamicParams=false. Explicit resource pages: reviews/faqs. Status page: quote-result. No catch-all or blog route exists.

## Part B — Proposed schema plan

Use **Page folder → Section items**, since no Studio pattern exists. One fixed-ID page document per current URL (29 editorial plus operational quote status = 30); add page.blog for the new landing. Page has route identity and ordered references to pageSection singleton documents. Each child has owner reference, stable sectionKey and explicit sectionType with typed content objects. Suggested fixed IDs: page.<existing-id>, section.<page-id>.<section-key>; preserve current source IDs, never derive IDs from editable titles. SEO Settings, Banner Section, each render-ordered section and Closing CTA are child editor items. Global blocks use references. Blog collections and protected submissions are separate lists.

Studio items open explicit documentId editors. Hide singleton types from ordinary new-document templates/lists, remove duplicate/delete actions where appropriate, validate ownership/order and query deterministic IDs. Structure UI alone is not access control or uniqueness enforcement. New route slugs must be reviewed against reserved URLs. Replace English title/eyebrow regex layout selection with explicit sectionType; migrate semantic metrics/cards/reviews/FAQ arrays rather than fragile text slicing.

Every editorial image uses accessibleImage: Sanity type image with options.hotspot=true, fields alt:string, decorative:boolean, optional caption/credit. Alt title **Alt text**; description exactly: **Describe the image for people who cannot see it. Leave empty only for decorative images.** Require non-empty alt unless decorative; require asset where the section requires an image. Applies to hero, closing, cards, gallery, logo, OG, Google icon, authors and Portable Text/video poster images. Decorative backgrounds may have empty alt by explicit choice; do not invent alt automatically. Use @sanity/image-url on the full image with crop/hotspot; derive dimensions/aspect/LQIP from asset metadata; next/image gets responsive sizes and Sanity alt. Restrict remotePatterns to approved project/dataset paths on cdn.sanity.io. Remove object-right cropping where it overrides editorial hotspot. Fonts and technical SVG icon glyphs remain code assets.

Repeating items are arrays of named object types with stable _key: cards preview title+summary/image; FAQ preview question; testimonial preview author+body; action preview label+href; gallery preview image+alt/caption. Use references for shared testimonials/catalog. Convert pipe-separated strings to arrays. Plain headings use string; multi-line plain descriptions use text; formatted prose/inline links use Portable Text.

## Part D — Active forms

Search covered <form, onSubmit, fetch(, formAction, action= and use server in src. **1 distinct active form: Quote request**, src/components/contact/quote-form.tsx. Inline on /contact/ through ContactSection; site-wide popup through QuoteModal mounted by HeaderNavigation in normal root layout. Header, hero, section, homepage closing and mobile #quote links open the same popup. Footer itself has mailto/phone/map links, not a separate form. Global-error has self-contained HTML and no header popup. No newsletter, upload, server action or direct browser-to-third-party form.

| Payload key | HTML type | Required / validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | input text | Required; trimmed 2–100 chars. |
| phone | input tel | Required; 7–30 chars; allowed phone symbols and at least 7 digits. |
| email | input email | Required; email validation, max 254. |
| message | textarea | Optional; empty permitted; non-empty 10–4000 chars. minLength does not make empty required. |
| website | CSS-hidden text honeypot | No required attribute; schema requires submitted empty string (max 0); filled bots rejected. Do not persist. |
| idempotencyToken | hidden input | Client UUID after hydration, empty with no JS; handler accepts optional string 0–80 alphanumeric/hyphen. Not in QuoteSchema parsed output. |
| vehicle | NOT rendered | Optional enum in QuoteSchema only, not an active form field; do not add silently. |

JS submits JSON fetch to POST /api/quote; progressive enhancement posts urlencoded/multipart using method=post action=/api/quote. Handler redirects native posts 303 to /quote-result/?state=success|error; JSON returns success/error. Server validates then forwards JSON to configured HTTPS webhook, not a browser third-party post. Message validation copy says required while UI/schema allow empty; choose copy correction or requirement change with approval. No consent checkbox or marketing opt-in exists; do not invent consent in stored records.

## Part E — Email / Resend

No repository email send exists. src/app/api/quote/route.ts uses QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL and optional QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET; external downstream provider, sender, recipients, subject and template are unknown. A webhook may email externally, but it was not contacted. Resend is not installed or imported. Mailto links are not server email.

Boundary evidence in handler: origin/host checks lines 22–26; streamed 16KB body limit/parsing lines 27–48; QuoteSchema validation lines 49–50; token validation 51–53; hash/dedupe 54–58. Delivery configuration begins **line 59**, HTTPS target check line 63, delivery promise line 64, external fetch 66–78; final await/result 81–83. Preserve all validation and public JSON/native-redirect contracts.

Proposal: install resend, server-only src/lib/forms/resend.ts and src/lib/forms/quote-email.tsx. Required env NAMES only: RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM_EMAIL, RESEND_TO_EMAIL. Require configured sender/recipients from env, verify sender domain before launch; never hardcode addresses. Visitor email can be replyTo only. React template escapes name/phone/email/message, adds UTC timestamp formatted in Pacific/Auckland and sanitized source pathname; provide plain-text equivalent. Controlled subject New quote enquiry (optionally sanitized/limited name). Do not expose provider error details or PII in logs; inspect SDK returned error as well as thrown errors.

If existing webhook is configured, preserve that workflow and do not add Resend alongside it (duplicate email risk). Where no webhook exists and Resend is configured, use Resend as the alternative delivery branch with the current idempotency hash; if neither exists retain 503/unconfigured. Existing external email, if confirmed, stays untouched; storage can be added independently. Replacing a downstream email workflow requires explicit approval. No autoresponder email proposed.

## Part F — Form submissions to Sanity

Referer: standard Request exposes request.headers.get("referer") if supplied; current handler never reads it. It may be missing or forged. Validate same-site source against canonical/request approved origin; persist pathname only, strip query/hash, never use as authentication. No current source field. Optional hidden sourcePath could improve popup attribution but requires separate validation; absence must not break no-JS flow.

Next package range ^15.5.0, lock resolved **15.5.28**. Local node_modules/next/server.d.ts exports after; available/stable since 15.1. import { after } from "next/server" is supported. after is lifecycle-bounded post-response work, not a durable queue or delivery guarantee. Store critical submissions before reporting success, or use a durable outbox.

Timezone: Christchurch NZ address; no IANA timezone in config. Proposed **Pacific/Auckland** inferred from address. Store UTC submittedAt and timezone separately; format with Intl/timeZone for daylight saving. Report date remains Asia/Calcutta; opening-hour calendar dates must not shift.

Only .env.example exists locally. Names there: QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL, QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CONTENT_SOURCE, SANITY_PROJECT_ID, SANITY_DATASET, SANITY_API_TOKEN, PAYLOAD_API_URL, PAYLOAD_API_KEY, BUILD_STANDALONE. Code additionally uses CONTENT_STRICT, VERCEL, VERCEL_ENV, CHECK_ORIGIN. Values are not reproduced. .gitignore ignores .env* and explicitly allows !.env.example, plus dependencies/build/tsbuildinfo. Keep examples blank and real credentials deployment-only. No formSubmission schema, lib/forms directory, write client, submissions database or durable queue exists. Existing 10-minute/1000-entry Map is process-local dedupe, not a durable limiter.

| formSubmission field | Type / required | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| formName | string R | quote |
| name / phone / email | string R | Only validated payload fields |
| message | text O | Empty allowed under present schema |
| vehicle | string O | Only if genuinely supplied/validated; not rendered today |
| submittedAt | datetime R | UTC server timestamp |
| timezone | string R | Pacific/Auckland |
| sourcePath | string O | Sanitized same-site pathname; nullable/missing allowed |
| idempotencyHash | string R | Derived digest, never raw request/secret |
| deliveryProvider | enum R | webhook/resend |
| deliveryStatus | enum R | pending/sent/failed/unknown; webhook acceptance not proof of email |
| emailStatus | enum R | pending/sent/failed/notApplicable/unknown; notApplicable or unknown for opaque webhook |
| providerMessageId / deliveredAt | string O / datetime O | Only safe identifiers/timestamps |
| retryCount / lastAttemptAt / leaseExpiresAt | number O / datetime O / datetime O | Durable claim/reconciliation as needed |

**Security blocker:** submissions must not be in a public-readable content dataset. Use private SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET or separate private project, server-only least-privilege SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN separate from read SANITY_API_TOKEN. No NEXT_PUBLIC write token. Studio submissions view needs separate private workspace/dataset and authorized staff; readOnly schema fields are not access control. Do not store raw headers, full Referer, IP, user-agent, honeypot, token, endpoint or provider error body. Approve retention/deletion and privacy policy before launch.

Use deterministic private ID formSubmission.quote.<hash> with createIfNotExists; record validated data before send; use durable atomic claim/lease/outbox for cross-instance dedupe. Reuse provider idempotency key. Distinguish stored-but-unsent, sent-but-status-update-failed and duplicate cases. Keep success tied to acknowledged provider delivery, not merely a saved record. Sanity and mail/webhook cannot be one transaction. If persistence is mandatory and fails, fail before send unless an explicit fallback is approved. after may perform bounded best-effort status reconciliation/queue wakeup after durable work exists, with caught/redacted errors; never put the only submission save into after. A durable retry strategy is still required for strict guarantees.

## Part G — Security

No hardcoded API key/token/private key detected in current tracked textual source/config/docs using common provider prefixes, private-key markers and literal secret assignments. **Candidate file/line locations: none.** No secret values were printed or written. This heuristic current-tree scan does not cover Git history, remote deployment settings or every binary/ignored file. Public business contact email, Google map embed and review-share URL are not secret credentials.

Further findings: missing Origin is permitted; host-only equality is a limited check, not abuse protection. Add shared server-side rate limiting before paid email/storage. Preserve honeypot/body limits, timeout and HTTPS/no-redirect webhook rules. Content queries must exclude submission types even with private data. Enforce server-only import boundaries; current repository imported by client code bundles local data and pulls CMS module dependency graph. Keep write client unimportable by browser. Validate rich-text links/protocols and video embeds; never execute stored HTML/code. Public errors generic; logs contain identifiers/status only. CMS indexing settings must not override preview/alias noindex safety.

const endpoint = process.env.QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL;
const resendReady = Boolean(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY && process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL && process.env.RESEND_TO_EMAIL);
if (!endpoint && !resendReady) return reply(503, content.form.messages.unconfigured);
if (deliveries.size >= 1000) return reply(429, content.form.messages.error);
const target = endpoint ? new URL(endpoint) : undefined;
if (target && target.protocol !== 'https:') throw new Error('Delivery endpoint must use HTTPS');
const send = target ? async () => {
  const response = await fetch(target, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Idempotency-Key': key,
      ...(process.env.QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET}` } : {}),
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(result.data),
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10000),
    redirect: 'error',
  });
  return { success: response.ok };
} : () => sendQuoteEmail(result.data, { key, sourcePath });
const delivery = processQuoteSubmission({
  key, values: result.data, sourcePath, timezone: 'Pacific/Auckland',
  provider: target ? 'webhook' : 'resend', send,
});
~~~

Keep existing Map registration/await/result behavior after this block; processQuoteSubmission returns Promise<boolean>, catches provider/storage errors without leaking values, and handles durable duplicate outcomes. A mere createIfNotExists without an atomic send claim is insufficient. Private save failure must not resolve success. Mail success but status-write failure requires reconciliation so retry does not duplicate mail. Webhook downstream must honor the same idempotency key for cross-instance retry guarantees.

Exact server-only Resend lines in new resend.ts (within async function, no module-load throw when webhook-only configuration is used):

~~~ts
import 'server-only';
import { Resend } from 'resend';
const apiKey = process.env.RESEND_API_KEY;
const from = process.env.RESEND_FROM_EMAIL;
const to = process.env.RESEND_TO_EMAIL?.split(',').map(value => value.trim()).filter(Boolean);
if (!apiKey || !from || !to?.length) return { success: false };
const resend = new Resend(apiKey);
const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({
  from, to, replyTo: values.email, subject: 'New quote enquiry',
  react: QuoteEmail({ values, submittedAt, sourcePath }),
  text: quoteEmailText({ values, submittedAt, sourcePath }),
}, { idempotencyKey: key });
return { success: !error && Boolean(data?.id), providerMessageId: data?.id };
~~~

Add typed imports/exports and bounded provider timeout/retry according to pinned SDK. Template uses React text nodes, not unsanitized HTML. Sender/recipients are exclusively env values. No mail was sent here.

Exact write-client guard lines:

~~~ts
import 'server-only';
import { createClient } from '@sanity/client';
const dataset = process.env.SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET;
const token = process.env.SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN;
if (!dataset || !token) throw new Error('Private submission storage is not configured');
export const submissionClient = createClient({
  projectId: process.env.SANITY_PROJECT_ID!, dataset, token,
  apiVersion: '2025-02-19', useCdn: false, perspective: 'published',
});
~~~

Dataset privacy must be verified administratively; a different dataset name alone does not ensure privacy. For webhook-only old deployments, lazily instantiate storage in the approved enabled path so unconfigured build imports do not crash unrelated pages. Feature flags, if used during rollout, must never silently claim saving is enabled while skipping it.

If after is used, exact import is `import { after } from 'next/server';`; use only after durable critical operations, e.g. `after(async () => { await reconcileDeliveryStatus(submissionId).catch(reportRedactedFailure); });`. No after-only persistence and no promise left unawaited outside lifecycle. Required durable work stays in processQuoteSubmission/outbox.

### Approval-gated verification later

During this audit no build, lint, tests or typecheck ran. The only allowed checker would have been npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false, but it was unnecessary for a report-only change. After implementation is approved, verify schema registration, migration dry-run totals/slugs/order/images/alt, public snapshot boundaries and all routes. Mock provider/storage responses for timeout/failure/duplicate/concurrency/no-JS/referrer-absent cases, canonical/robots/SEO and Portable Text object rendering. Ask separately before any real submission/email/CMS upload/import or deployment; never use customer PII in checks. Current instruction remains in force until changed.

### Risks / Blockers

1. No Studio/config/structure or account provisioned; need target project/datasets and roles. Existing schema templates are incomplete and do not enforce singleton identity.
2. Public dataset cannot contain private submissions; private dataset/access policy and least-privilege credentials are launch blockers.
3. Globals/gallery/catalog/form copy still local; switching CONTENT_SOURCE alone is incomplete. Client repository imports and module-scope synchronous configuration require a deliberate server/context boundary refactor.
4. Image shape, hotspot/crop and positive-dimension validation differ from current schema. Missing alt/caption rights need review; originals may include illustrative/editorial assets that must remain distinguished from real project photographs.
5. English regex/array positions control layouts; duplicate FAQ/review sources and omitted final sections can corrupt render parity if imported mechanically. Keep 313 logical section count as baseline.
6. Existing webhook may already send email; downstream provider/recipients/template/idempotency unknown. Resend domain verification and env sender/recipient configuration required when used.
7. Sanity + delivery cannot commit atomically; current Map and after cannot guarantee durability. Approve retry/outbox/queue and durable concurrency claim strategy before guaranteeing exactly-once/at-least-once outcomes.
8. New root slugs currently require rebuild. Revalidation and canonical-host middleware changes must preserve nonproduction/alias noindex. Studio/status/submission endpoints excluded from sitemap.
9. Blog has no source posts, categories or authors. Do not invent posts; approve taxonomy/layout and supply content.
10. No deployment/provider versions or permission tiers were tested; select compatible Studio/SDK packages without silent framework upgrade.
11. Form message-required copy conflicts with optional validation; response-time promise is unconfirmed; past holiday exception and rating claim require business review.
12. Secret scan is heuristic, not Git-history/deployment audit; no hardcoded credential candidates found in current tracked text.

### Needs approval

- Approve implementation of this plan and source/dependency changes; until then this remains a report.
- Approve target Sanity project, content/private submission datasets, Studio deployment/access roles, deterministic singleton migration and later uploads/import/publish operations.
- Approve public/private dataset separation, PII fields/retention/deletion/access policy, privacy copy and durable retry platform/failure policy.
- Confirm current webhook ownership/email behavior and whether Resend fallback is desired; approve verified sender domain and deployment-only sender/recipient configuration. No addresses are requested in source.
- Approve blog taxonomy/design/routes/content, optional tags/sidebar, and new navigation links.
- Approve any behavior change: on-demand root slugs, form message requirement, extra consent/source field, consolidation of the two homepage closing CTAs. Defaults preserve present behavior.
- Authorize real end-to-end sends, Sanity writes/imports and deployment separately when the concrete implementation is reviewable. None is authorized or performed by this audit.

Image paths include src/alt/width/height; future asset/crop/hotspot replaces storage details while preserving alt. ## Sanity Implementation

Implemented 17 November 2026. This entry supersedes the audit’s proposed-work status; the earlier report is historical. The latest instructions govern phase 5: additive, post-response saving replaces the earlier blocking/outbox proposal. No Sanity writes, import runs, submissions, email sends or deployment occurred.

### Phase-wise summary

1. Studio: /studio, fixed-ID Page → Section editors, eleven global singletons (the original ten plus the explicitly requested Sitemap), Blog Posts/taxonomy lists. Existing schema order is preserved; new definitions append. Singleton create templates and duplicate/delete actions are excluded. Local initial values do not seed a dataset.
2. Pages: server-only published GROQ with 60-second revalidation, validated DTOs, token-free client context and field-level source fallbacks. Current sections/globals/catalog/gallery/testimonials/CTA/SEO/recovery content is connected. Stable IDs retain layout dispatch; unused final service/about source sections are not exposed. Optional Payload mode remains.
3. Images: image/hotspot/Alt text fields, @sanity/image-url, next/image and CDN remotePatterns. Local images/variants/alt remain fallbacks. No uploads occurred.
4. Blog: post/category/author/tag schemas; Blog Page SEO/banner/filter/featured/sidebar/internal/footer CTA controls; list/detail, Portable Text Image/Video/Table/Callout/Divider/Code, SEO/BlogPosting, sitemap and signed publication refresh. No legacy posts existed, so no conditional import-blog script is needed or created; no import command applies.
5. Forms: quote registry, lazy bounded writer, non-mutating saver, Pacific/Auckland dates, status-only editing and live Year/Month counts. Resend HTML/text/reply-to runs only without a configured webhook; the existing webhook body/auth/timeout/redirect are preserved.

Each phase passed `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false` after corrections; final integration check also exited 0. No build, lint or tests ran. Existing metadata test call sites were adjusted for async robots and Studio exclusion but not executed. Missing packages were installed with --ignore-scripts; Next.js was not upgraded.

### Design and form preservation

Existing layout classes, CSS, section order, both homepage closing panels, inputs, validation schema, honeypot, payload, JSON success/conversion behavior and native POST 303 redirect destinations are preserved. Context adds no DOM wrapper. CMS fields use identical current defaults. Browser/visual parity and real response timing were not exercised under the restrictions; the later client checklist covers these.

### Forms covered

| Form | Placements | Handler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quote request (quote), src/components/contact/quote-form.tsx | Inline /contact/; global popup from header/mobile/hero/section/closing CTAs | src/app/api/quote/route.ts |

Saving uses Next.js after following existing validation. No save is awaited on the response path. No token/project → silent skip. Storage never mutates result.data, email payload or response and never stores website/idempotencyToken. Limits: name 200, email 320, phone 100, message 10,000, sourcePage 2,048 (query/hash removed), extra label 100, extra value 4,000, max 50 extras. Saving is best effort, not a durable queue.

### Studio wiring

sanity.config.ts registers structureTool, the appended schema index and singleton filters. src/cms/sanity/structure.ts lists globals once, fixed-ID Page → Section items and Blog Posts, then appends formSubmissionsStructure at the END. No auto-generated duplicate singleton/Form Submission list.

Form Submissions → Quote request → Year (count) → Month (count) → entries, newest first. Form folder is always shown; only non-empty years/months appear. No All Submissions or day folders. Month filter: `_type == "formSubmission" && formType == $formType && submittedDate match $prefix`, prefix YYYY-MM*, via context.getClient API 2024-01-01.

For a separate private dataset, /studio/submissions is its workspace; the content workspace’s final Form Submissions item links there. With the shared default dataset, folders open directly.

### Vercel env vars

Default Studio/content dataset name: **production**. NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET must match Studio; server identifiers must match too. New .env.example names have blank values; .gitignore permits !.env.example. No real configuration was changed.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| CONTENT_SOURCE | Set sanity to enable CMS reads; local retains current content. |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID | Public Studio project identifier; match server project. |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET | Public Studio dataset, default production. |
| SANITY_PROJECT_ID / SANITY_DATASET | Server identifiers, matching Studio. |
| SANITY_API_TOKEN | Optional private reader and fallback writer; needs Editor permission if used to write. Server-only. |
| SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN | Optional dedicated writer, falls back to SANITY_API_TOKEN; needs Editor permission. Server-only. |
| SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET | Optional write override; fallback NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET, then SANITY_DATASET, then production. |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET | Public identifier for separate private workspace; match SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET. Not a token. |
| SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET | Server-only signed publish webhook verification at /api/revalidate. |
| SITE_CANONICAL_URL | Canonical indexing host; current domain is fallback. |
| QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL / QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET | Existing delivery variables, retained with precedence. |
| RESEND_API_KEY | Server-only no-webhook email fallback key. |
| RESEND_FROM_EMAIL | Verified sender from env only. |
| RESEND_TO_EMAIL | Recipient(s) from env only; comma separated if multiple. |

All three Resend variables are required for fallback delivery. Reply-to is the submitter, never From. Never use NEXT_PUBLIC for any token/key. Writer: apiVersion 2024-01-01, useCdn false, timeout 3000, maxRetries 0.

### Privacy note

Submissions contain personal data. Limit dataset access to authorised staff; use a separate private dataset or restrict the default production dataset before storage. readOnly is only a Studio UI setting, not access control. Configure Sanity roles/API permissions and agree retention/deletion/privacy policy before real collection. Logs omit payloads, request objects and credentials. No permissions were changed.

### Needs approval

- Real Sanity/Vercel setup: project/datasets, privacy/roles, Editor permission, Studio/CORS and env configuration.
- Sender-domain verification and intended recipients; confirm existing webhook notification ownership.
- Personal-data retention/deletion policy and public privacy wording.
- Later live submissions/emails, uploads/publication, webhook setup and deployment, expressly prohibited in this implementation.
- Further form fields/validation, design changes, new generic page slugs, durable queue/retry infrastructure or future legacy blog imports require separate scope approval.

### Security findings

None detected.

### Client content-fill checklist

- Business & Contact: contact/address, founding year, rating, weekly/holiday hours and response-time guidance.
- Branding: upload logo/badge/shared images, set hotspot and alt/decorative choices.
- Header / Footer: vehicle/main/legal/social/credit links and map.
- SEO / Sitemap: canonical, OG/business image, SEO text, exclusions/priorities; preview/alias safeguards remain.
- CTA / Quote Form / Interface & Recovery: labels/targets, privacy/status text, gallery/carousel/accessibility/recovery copy. Field definitions and validation stay in code.
- Catalog / Testimonials: verify five vehicle groups/images and shared review text/authors.
- Every Page: review Settings, SEO, Banner, displayed sections and Closing CTA. FAQs use source section records, then aggregate. Current defaults are already supplied.
- Upload page banner/closing, comparison/workshop, service/benefit/card and gallery images with alt; distinguish illustrations from real project photos. Existing files remain.
- Blog Page: SEO/banner/filter/featured/sidebar/CTA settings and labels; create real categories/authors/posts with date, excerpt, featured image/alt and body. No posts were fabricated.
- Confirm private submissions dataset/workspace and authorised staff before enabling the writer.

### How to test later — not performed

**WARNING: each test submit also sends the real notification email. Inform the recipient beforehand and use the name “TEST DELETE ME”.**

1. Configure approved env settings. Compare each page/device to the old design, including mobile navigation, gallery, both homepage closing panels, popup focus/dismissal and footer.
2. Change an image and Alt text in Studio, publish, confirm image/alt/hotspot after cache refresh; check fallbacks.
3. Publish a test blog post with category/author/image/alt and each body object. Check list/detail/filter/sidebar/related/SEO/sitemap and draft/future exclusion. Remove it afterwards.
4. Submit inline /contact/ and every popup placement: header/mobile/hero/section/closing. Verify JS success and native POST redirect.
5. Studio → Form Submissions → Quote request → Year → Month: newest record on top with Pacific/Auckland date/time. Year/month folders appear only after a record exists. Open the private workspace first for an override dataset.
6. Confirm notification/reply-to, saved fields and no honeypot/token data; verify thank-you/redirect speed unchanged. Saving is asynchronous, so allow it to finish. Only status is editable.
7. Delete all TEST DELETE ME records afterwards and confirm counts/folders refresh. Remove test posts/assets under owner policy. No live test data was created here.

**sanity.config.ts**

~~~ts
import { defineConfig, type WorkspaceOptions } from 'sanity';
import { structureTool } from 'sanity/structure';
import { schemaTypes, singletonTypes } from './src/cms/sanity/schemaTypes';
import { formSubmission } from './src/cms/sanity/schemaTypes/form-submission';
import { websiteStructure } from './src/cms/sanity/structure';
import { formSubmissionsStructure } from './sanity/structure/formSubmissionsStructure';
const dataset = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET || 'production';
const submissionsDataset = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET || dataset;
const projectId = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID || 'unconfigured';
const website: WorkspaceOptions = {
  name: 'website', title: 'JL Coachbuilders', basePath: submissionsDataset === dataset ? '/studio' : '/studio/website',
  projectId, dataset, plugins: [structureTool({ structure: websiteStructure })], schema: { types: schemaTypes },
  document: {
    newDocumentOptions: templates => templates.filter(template => !singletonTypes.has(template.templateId) && template.templateId !== 'formSubmission'),
    actions: (actions, context) => singletonTypes.has(context.schemaType)
      ? actions.filter(action => action.action !== 'delete' && action.action !== 'duplicate')
      : actions,
  },
};
export default defineConfig(submissionsDataset === dataset ? website : [website, {
  name: 'submissions', title: 'Private submissions', basePath: '/studio/submissions',
  projectId, dataset: submissionsDataset, schema: { types: [formSubmission] },
  plugins: [structureTool({ structure: (S, context) => S.list().title('Private submissions').items([formSubmissionsStructure(S, context)]) })],
  document: { newDocumentOptions: () => [] },
}]);
~~~

~~~ts
import type { SchemaTypeDefinition } from 'sanity';
import { sanitySchemaTypes } from '../schema';
import { globalTypes } from './globals';
import { pageTypes } from './pages';
import { blogTypes } from './blog';
import { objectTypes } from './objects';
import { formSubmission } from './form-submission';
// Keep the existing schema order intact; new definitions are appended.
export const schemaTypes = [...sanitySchemaTypes, ...globalTypes, ...pageTypes, ...objectTypes, ...blogTypes, formSubmission] as SchemaTypeDefinition[];
export const singletonTypes = new Set([...globalTypes.map(type => type.name), ...pageTypes.map(type => type.name), ...blogTypes.filter(type => type.name.startsWith('blog') && !['blogPost', 'blogCategory', 'blogAuthor', 'blogTag'].includes(type.name)).map(type => type.name), 'page', 'siteSettings', 'quoteFormContent']);
~~~


**src/cms/sanity/structure.ts**

~~~ts
import type { StructureResolver, StructureBuilder } from 'sanity/structure';
import defaults from './defaults.json';
import { formSubmissionsStructure } from '../../../sanity/structure/formSubmissionsStructure';
const document = (S: StructureBuilder, item: { id: string; type: string; title: string }) =>
  S.listItem().id(item.id).title(item.title).child(S.document().schemaType(item.type).documentId(item.id));
export const websiteStructure: StructureResolver = (S, context) => S.list().title('Website').items([
  ...defaults.globals.map(item => document(S, item)),
  ...defaults.registry.map(page => S.listItem().id(page.id).title(page.title).child(
    S.list().title(page.title).items(page.items.map(item => document(S, item)))
  )),
  ...['blogCategory', 'blogAuthor', 'blogTag'].map(type => S.listItem().title({ blogCategory: 'Blog Categories', blogAuthor: 'Blog Authors', blogTag: 'Blog Tags' }[type]!).child(S.documentTypeList(type))),
  S.listItem().title('Blog Posts').schemaType('blogPost').child(S.documentTypeList('blogPost').title('Blog Posts')),
  formSubmissionsStructure(S, context),
]);
~~~


**sanity/structure/formSubmissionsStructure.ts**

~~~ts
import type { StructureBuilder, StructureResolverContext } from 'sanity/structure';
import { map, startWith, switchMap } from 'rxjs';
import { FORMS } from '../../src/lib/forms/config';
import { SubmissionsWorkspaceLink } from './SubmissionsWorkspaceLink';
const apiVersion = '2024-01-01';
export function formSubmissionsStructure(S: StructureBuilder, context: StructureResolverContext) {
  const dataset = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET || process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET || 'production';
  const root = S.listItem().id('form-submissions').title('Form Submissions');
  if (dataset !== context.dataset) return root.child(S.component().id('private-submissions').title('Form Submissions').component(SubmissionsWorkspaceLink));
  const client = context.getClient({ apiVersion }).withConfig({ perspective: 'published' });
  const dates = (formType: string) => {
    const query = '_type == "formSubmission" && formType == $formType && defined(submittedDate)';
    return client.observable.listen('*[' + query + ']', { formType }, { events: ['welcome', 'mutation'], includeResult: false }).pipe(
      startWith(null),
      switchMap(() => client.observable.fetch<{ submittedDate: string }[]>('*[' + query + ']{submittedDate}', { formType })),
      map(items => items.map(item => item.submittedDate).filter(value => /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value))),
    );
  };
  return root.child(S.list().title('Form Submissions').items(FORMS.map(form =>
    S.listItem().id(form.id).title(form.title).child(() => dates(form.id).pipe(map(values => {
      const years = [...new Set(values.map(value => value.slice(0, 4)))].sort().reverse();
      return S.list().id('years-' + form.id).title(form.title).items(years.map(year => {
        const count = values.filter(value => value.startsWith(year + '-')).length;
        return S.listItem().id(form.id + '-' + year).title(year + ' (' + count + ')').child(() => dates(form.id).pipe(map(current => {
          const inYear = current.filter(value => value.startsWith(year + '-'));
          const months = [...new Set(inYear.map(value => value.slice(0, 7)))].sort().reverse();
          return S.list().id('months-' + form.id + '-' + year).title(year).items(months.map(month => {
            const monthName = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-NZ', { month: 'long', timeZone: 'UTC' }).format(new Date(month + '-15T12:00:00Z'));
            const monthCount = inYear.filter(value => value.startsWith(month)).length;
            return S.listItem().id(form.id + '-' + month).title(monthName + ' (' + monthCount + ')').child(
              S.documentList().id('entries-' + form.id + '-' + month).title(monthName + ' ' + year)
                .schemaType('formSubmission').apiVersion(apiVersion)
                .filter('_type == "formSubmission" && formType == $formType && submittedDate match $prefix')
                .params({ formType: form.id, prefix: month + '*' })
                .defaultOrdering([{ field: 'submittedAt', direction: 'desc' }])
            );
          }));
        })));
      }));
    })))
  )));
}
~~~

<details><summary>docs/cms-integration.md</summary>

~~~text
1: # Sanity CMS integration
3: The website has an embedded Sanity Studio at /studio, fixed page/section editors, server-side published-content reads and source-backed defaults. No dataset has been provisioned or written by this implementation.
5: ## Configuration
7: Copy .env.example to an ignored .env.local or set deployment environment variables. Set CONTENT_SOURCE=sanity to enable CMS reads. Without configured identifiers, or when a CMS field is empty/unavailable, the current local content remains visible.
9: The default dataset name is **production**. Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET for Studio. SANITY_PROJECT_ID and SANITY_DATASET, when supplied for server reads, must match those same identifiers. Use SANITY_API_TOKEN only on the server if private content requires authentication. Public identifiers are not tokens.
11: Studio shows eleven global singletons, page folders with section items, Blog Posts/Categories/Authors/Tags and Form Submissions at the end. Existing schema registrations retain their original order. New singleton templates are excluded from the normal create menu; duplicate/delete actions are removed for fixed singleton documents. Initial editor values come from src/cms/sanity/defaults.json; these templates do not write anything until an authorised editor explicitly saves/publishes.
13: Editors for service/about final source sections omitted by the live template are not exposed. FAQs are edited in their source section, then aggregated; testimonials are shared. Existing slugs/layouts remain fixed. New generic content routes are not automatically added.
15: ## Images
17: Upload images through the image fields. Every image supports hotspot and Alt text. Meaningful images need alt; decorative images can be marked decorative. Existing local images remain the fallback. The server resolves asset references with @sanity/image-url and the front end uses next/image. No existing assets were uploaded automatically.
19: ## Blog
21: /blog/ lists published articles and /blog/[slug]/ shows a post. Create a category and author, then a Blog Post with title, slug, publication date, excerpt, featured image/alt and Portable Text body. Future-dated posts/drafts stay private. Blog Page contains SEO, banner, filter/featured selections, list/detail labels, optional sidebar, internal CTA and footer CTA. There were no legacy posts, so no blog import script or import run is needed.
23: Publish changes are visible after the 60-second cache window. For immediate refresh, configure a signed Sanity webhook to POST /api/revalidate using SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET. Its projection should include _type, _id, slug and beforeSlug when a post slug changes. No webhook was configured or invoked here. Arbitrary paths and submission document events are rejected.
25: ## Quote delivery and submission storage
27: The same QuoteForm remains inline on /contact/ and in the global popup. Fields, validation, honeypot, native-post redirects and JSON success/conversion behavior are preserved.
29: If QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL is configured, its existing HTTPS delivery flow/auth/body remain in use. Resend is used only when no webhook is configured and RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM_EMAIL and RESEND_TO_EMAIL are all set. The sender must have a verified domain; recipient values come from env and reply-to is the validated submitter. No message was sent during implementation.
31: Validated submissions are saved using Next.js after, outside the response path. Storage failure never changes the email or response. This is best-effort saving, not a durable queue. SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN is optional and falls back to SANITY_API_TOKEN; the writer requires Editor permission. With no token/project, saving silently does nothing.
33: The write dataset resolves SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET, then NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET, then SANITY_DATASET, then production. For a separate private dataset, set SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET to the same name. Studio provides a separate private workspace and the content workspace links to it at Form Submissions. With no override, submissions are stored in production: restrict that dataset's read access before enabling storage.
35: Studio hierarchy: Form Submissions → Quote request → Year (count) → Month (count) → records, newest first. Form folder is always shown; year/month folders appear only with records. Only status is editable; test records can still be deleted through document actions.
37: **Privacy:** submissions contain personal data. Limit dataset access to authorised staff. readOnly controls Studio UI only, not API access. Agree retention/deletion and privacy policy before accepting real enquiries. Never expose a write token in NEXT_PUBLIC variables.
39: ## Verification authorised for this implementation
41: Only npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false was run. Build, lint, tests, live submissions, email sends, dataset mutations, imports and deployment were not run. See Changes/Aditya_17-11-26.md under Sanity Implementation for the file-level record and client checks.
~~~

## Sanity Completion Verification

Date: 17 November 2026. Read the Sanity Audit Report, Implementation Plan and Sanity Implementation before this pass. The prior completion claims were not accepted as evidence. This entry records source inspection and corrections; it does not certify a deployed Studio or successful CMS/email round trip.

### Verified counts and limits

- Original scope: **30 page URLs / 313 logical page sections**. The 29 local content records comprise home, 21 service pages, about, contact, two legal pages, gallery, reviews and FAQs; quote-result is the 30th URL. The root dynamic route handles 26 content records; home/reviews/FAQs/status are explicit pages.
- Stored source sections: **251**, not 313. Heroes, closing panels, three additional introductions, FAQ aggregation and omitted terminal source sections explain the difference. The new map explicitly counts 22 FAQ topic sections, one reviews grid and one status panel. Contact map/hours remain inside location; decorative dividers and CTA rows are nested; the root homepage-only closing panel remains a global.
- Global singleton count: **11** — business, branding, header, footer, SEO, separate Sitemap, shared CTA, Quote Form, interface/recovery copy, vehicle catalog and testimonials. They appear once at the top level.
- The added /blog list makes **31 fixed public page URLs** in source, plus a dynamic /blog/[slug] template. There are no local legacy posts; remote published post count is unverified. /studio catch-all and metadata/API endpoints are separate admin/system surfaces, not included in the 30/313 baseline.
- All **313 baseline section identities** have mapped editor IDs, projections/helpers and render consumption in source. This is source coverage, not proof of populated documents or published updates; real Studio/browser round trips remain unverified.

### Missing work found and corrected

1. Three rendered introduction sections had no own editor; now contentIntroduction documents feed page.introduction.
2. The 22 aggregated FAQ topics lacked page-level editors; now fixed faqTopicSection documents can override their topic copy/answers while falling back to source-page FAQs. The unused standalone copied FAQ set is not offered as an active topic.
3. The reviews grid had no editor/selection path; now reviewGridSection controls selection and its region label without duplicating the global testimonial owner.
4. Home controls were scattered into the banner, and some exposed fields were ignored. Owning sections now expose intro/metrics/assurances/service cards/help card/checklists/capabilities/comparison/review selection/actions. Raw copied fields are hidden where superseded.
5. Main prose now uses explicit bodyBlocks after removing duplicate source leads/related-link copies. Rich inline fields and links reach existing paragraph/heading wrappers. Introduction/link-array schema inference was corrected for empty default arrays.
6. Editable headings were still involved in dispatch and metric recognition. Layout, CTA placement and source icon identity now come from layout-map.json; metrics are structured fields.
7. Empty/type-invalid content could wipe valid sibling edits or remove fixed home defaults. mergeContent and validateContent now preserve field-level defaults and reject invalid new array items, with semantic defaults retained for the renderers.
8. Caption/decorative/hotspot data was stripped/ignored in places. It now survives image normalization and reaches the no-wrapper next/image adapter; original-image links and local optimisation variants are retained.
9. Blog curated ordering, sidebar limits, author/tag content, poster/tone data, CTA destinations and listing noindex behavior had gaps; these are wired through projection/normalizer/render paths.
10. The asset generator now updates src/content/web-manifest.json instead of recreating a conflicting public/site.webmanifest file; it was not run. Status SEO was mixed with status copy; it has a dedicated SEO editor. /site.webmanifest was static; it is now a read-only CMS-backed route with the same URL and former defaults. Viewport colour and root SEO defaults are wired.
11. Legacy globals/fields whose edits were overridden or unused are hidden instead of being advertised as live controls. Existing form validation, inputs, payloads, webhook and response flows were left unchanged.

### Complete route → section → schema/editor → query/helper → rendered field mapping

**Q1**, used in every baseline row: `export const singletonQuery = '*[_id in $ids && !(_id in path("drafts.**"))]{...}';` at src/lib/sanity/queries.ts:1. `$ids` is the fixed seed-ID list, including each listed document. This is an explicit published-document projection, not a claim based only on schema registration.

**H1**: src/lib/sanity/public-content.ts:18 resolves the document by fixed ID, merges local defaults, resolves images and validates the public shape. src/content/merge.ts:2 and src/content/validate.ts:2 define fallback handling. Client renderers receive the public DTO through src/components/providers/site-content.tsx; tokens are not passed.

**S1**: src/cms/sanity/schemaTypes/pages.ts:3 plus src/cms/sanity/schemaTypes/section-fields.ts:6 define the shared field structures and document-specific visibility; src/cms/sanity/schemaTypes/completion.ts:4 defines the new introduction/topic/grid types. Each row also points at its concrete seed/initial-value fields in defaults.json; shared schema reuse alone is not the completion criterion.

### Exact remaining external setup steps

1. Select the real Sanity project and confirm its content dataset. The source fallback name is production. Set matching NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID/NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET and, if used, matching server SANITY_PROJECT_ID/SANITY_DATASET. Set CONTENT_SOURCE=sanity to explicitly select CMS reads.
2. Create/choose a restricted submissions dataset (for example, submissions is a suggestion, not an account fact). Set SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET to that exact name; this enables the private workspace link. If using production for submissions, restrict its read access first.
3. Give authorised staff appropriate Studio access. Configure a server-only Editor-capable SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN for the target dataset, or deliberately use the SANITY_API_TOKEN fallback with the required permission. Never expose either token with NEXT_PUBLIC.
4. Add only the actual Studio origins in Sanity CORS: the chosen production HTTPS origin, authorised preview origins and the selected local development origin when needed. Allow authenticated Studio access only as required; do not use wildcard credential origins.
5. Configure Vercel variables for the intended environments, including canonical origin. Confirm public/server content identifiers and private workspace/write dataset identifiers match. No values were entered here.
6. Keep existing QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL/SECRET if it already notifies the owner. Only for the no-webhook fallback, verify the Resend sender domain via the owner’s DNS/account, set RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM_EMAIL and RESEND_TO_EMAIL, and confirm intended recipients. No email was sent.
7. Configure a signed Sanity publish webhook to /api/revalidate with SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET, publishing only relevant content types; include _type/_id/slug and beforeSlug on slug changes. This webhook was not configured or invoked.
8. Open the configured Studio, review initial values and fill/publish authorised content. Initial values are templates; no seed/import was executed. Run the later authorised browser/CMS checks before deployment. No deploy command is included as an action performed here.

## Environment Simplification

17 November 2026. Inspected actual environment usages in CMS readers/adapters, image resolution, Studio/CLI, submission storage, email delivery, signed revalidation, middleware, Next config, Docker and optional provider/tooling paths before editing. The owner confirmed **Resend** is the active notification provider; this was user confirmation, not a live delivery/account check.

### Minimal configuration

The blank .env.example now contains exactly nine names:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| CONTENT_SOURCE | Choose local or sanity; existing payload mode remains supported separately. |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID | One public project identifier for Studio, content, images and CLI. |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET | One public content dataset identifier; production remains the default. |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET | Public identifier for the private submissions workspace. |
| SANITY_SUBMISSIONS_DATASET | Writer target; must match the private workspace name and differ from the content dataset. |
| SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN | Server-only submission writer with the required private-dataset permission. |
| RESEND_API_KEY | Existing Resend server credential. |
| RESEND_FROM_EMAIL | Existing verified sender, taken only from environment. |
| RESEND_TO_EMAIL | Existing notification recipient(s), taken only from environment. |

### Code and compatibility changes

- Added src/lib/sanity/config.ts:2: shared public-first project/dataset resolution. Active reads, image URLs, CLI and legacy Sanity adapters use it. No duplicate SANITY_PROJECT_ID/SANITY_DATASET values are required. Those aliases remain backward-compatible only when public identifiers are absent; new setups should not configure them.

- Public content requests remain token-free when SANITY_API_TOKEN is absent. Private-content authenticated reads and the old server-only writer-token fallback are retained for compatibility, documented separately rather than required by the minimal example.

- sanity/lib/writeClient.ts:9: removed the writer’s unsafe content-dataset fallback. Saving skips when private dataset names are absent/mismatched or equal the content dataset. Existing lazy/after-response saving and its API version/timeout/retry settings remain. This protects against accidental content-dataset writes; real dataset privacy/access roles still require owner verification.

- Existing Resend sender/recipient/reply-to, subject, HTML/text template and quote webhook precedence/authentication/payload are unchanged. No email-handler or form source was edited in this pass. QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL and QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET remain supported if an existing deployment uses that alternative; no live variable was deleted or changed.

### Removed from the minimal example, not blindly removed from support

| Optional setting | Why it is separate / retained behavior |
| --- | --- |
| SANITY_PROJECT_ID / SANITY_DATASET | Deprecated duplicate identifiers; public names take precedence, aliases retained for existing server-only setups. |
| SANITY_API_TOKEN | Only needed for private content reads or legacy writer-token compatibility; public content requires no token. New submission setup uses SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN. |
| QUOTE_WEBHOOK_URL / QUOTE_WEBHOOK_SECRET | Alternative notification provider, not the owner-confirmed active Resend setup. Branch and authentication remain unchanged. |
| PAYLOAD_API_URL / PAYLOAD_API_KEY | Required only when explicitly selecting the existing Payload provider; code support remains. |
| SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET | Optional signed publish-hook secret. Signature verification is unchanged; missing secret keeps that endpoint unavailable. Ordinary 60-second timed revalidation continues without it. |
| BUILD_STANDALONE | Docker sets this internally; its Next.js switch and Docker configuration remain unchanged. |
| SITE_CANONICAL_URL | Optional canonical-host override; existing tracked site URL remains the fallback. Middleware protection is unchanged. |

VERCEL/VERCEL_ENV remain platform-managed. CONTENT_STRICT and CHECK_ORIGIN remain optional tooling switches. No Docker, Vercel or account configuration was removed.

A different dataset name alone does not prove restricted access, and Studio readOnly is not access control.
